newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Thursday with most investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,408 yuan ($410.60) per tonne, losing one yuan. It opened at 3,416 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,418 and a low of 3,402 yuan.
May was unchanged at 3,360, September rose two to 3,447, November was up 12 to 3,450 and January 1998 contract fell 10 to 3,430 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 13,700 tonnes from 16,700 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved in narrow ranges for most of the session after rises in the past few days, traders said.
"Investors seemed to lose trading direction and most of them are waiting for fresh market-moving news," one trader said.
"Active trading in A shares in the afternoon also attracted lots of speculative funds from retail investors," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move at current levels for the next few days.
